title: Applications
text:
How can you use cyberinfrastructure resources to escalate your research?

Process bigger data, faster - CI gives you access to supercomputers and cloud systems that can crunch massive datasets in hours instead of weeks on a regular laptop.
Run complex simulations - Model weather systems, protein folding, traffic patterns, or any other large-scale scenario that would be impossible on standard hardware.
Store and manage large amounts of data - CI provides secure, large-scale storage so you’re not limited by a hard drive - and your data is backed up and accessible anywhere.
Collaborate across institutions - Share datasets, code, and results with research partners at other universities or organizations in real time, no matter where they are.
Access specialized software and tools - Many CI platforms come pre-loaded with scientific software, AI/ML frameworks, and analysis tools - no expensive licenses needed.
Scale up without buying hardware - Instead of purchasing servers, you can request computing time on national or institutional systems, saving your budget for actual research.
Train AI and machine learning models - CI systems with GPUs let you build and train models on large datasets - work that’s often out of reach for individual researchers otherwise.
Speed up your publication timeline - Faster computing = faster results = faster path to publishing and sharing your discoveries with the world.
Open doors to new research questions - When you’re no longer limited by computing power, you can ask bigger, bolder questions that simply weren’t possible before.

Maunalua Fishpond Heritage Center Dashboard
The Maunalua Fishpond Heritage Center Dashboard is an application created to monitor the variables of two fishponds, Kanewai and Kalauhaihai, in Hawaii Kai. The conditions of the ponds’ temperature, salinity, pH, and oxygen will be shown to users for education. We have used supercomputing resources to host this application on a Jetstream2 server in hopes to increase the performance of the dashboard.

title: Applications
text:
Classroom Use
How can cyberinfrastructure be applied in the classroom?

Give students access to real research tools - Instead of simplified software, students can work with the same powerful platforms and datasets that professional researchers use, making learning more relevant and hands-on.
Enable data-driven projects - Students can collect, store, and analyze real-world data for class projects - from climate trends to social patterns - building practical skills employers actually want.
Support collaborative assignments - Cloud-based CI tools let students work together across different locations, devices, and time zones, mirroring how modern research teams actually operate.
Bring simulations into the curriculum - Teachers can use CI-powered simulations to visually demonstrate complex concepts - like molecular structures, ecosystem changes, or engineering stress tests - making abstract ideas click.
Prepare students for research careers - Early exposure to supercomputing, data management, and scientific workflows gives students a competitive edge when applying for internships, graduate programs, or research positions.

title: Get Started
text: If you’re still unsure if these resources are right for you or how to use them, we have facilitation support available.

title: Get Started
text:
Steps to Get Started

Set up an initial consultation meeting
To schedule an initial consultation meeting, visit this link.
We ask that you prepare the following prior to the initial meeting: - Project/research purpose - # of participants in possible workshop - Current research/teaching methods and tools


Schedule a workshop for you or your classroom
After the initial consultation meeting, we’ll collaborate on workshop or lab material for you and your class to use. From there, we can schedule a time for us to come and run through the material.
For individual or group researchers, we’ll schedule virtual or in-person training sessions to help you best use these resources.
Please provide us 2 weeks lead time to prepare classroom workshop materials.


Review documentation
Check out this resource for more technical and detailed information on using some of the CI tools.

title: Research Cyberinfrastructure at Chaminade University
text:
Cyberinfrastructure (CI) is a system of people and technologies brought together to perform computational analyses of big data in order to achieve breakthrough science and solve large-scale problems.
In other words, CI involves high-performance computing (HPC), supercomputers, massive data storage and data management systems, specialized applications for modeling, simulation, and analysis, and experts and support staff who help develop and operate these systems.

title: Research Cyberinfrastructure at Chaminade University
text:
About Chaminade University
Chaminade University of Honolulu is part of the Cyberinfrastructure Pacific Professionals (CIPP) in partnership with University of Hawaii, University of Guam, and Texas Advanced Computing Center. CIPP is a collaborative initiative dedication to strengthening CI capabilities across the Hawaii/Guam and US Affiliated Pacific Islands region.
